claim_verdicts.claim: Claim 3: the bar (sortMin.abs=0.10) is a threshold, not a cost; EV 3.6848 -> 3.6781
claim_verdicts.reason: As a description of the code it holds exactly: bar 0 -> 3.6848 (+3.80%), bar 0.10 -> 3.6781 (+3.61%), Δ −0.0067/case, reproduced on the rendered page (page_check.txt bar0). But the page's own rationale for the bar (lines 4406-4414: 'the listing itself costs attention... five copper a listing') is a per-listing cost, and a cost is paid on every listing that clears the bar too. With fee 0.10 on the 0.379 listings/case that clear the bar the EV is 3.6402 = +2.54% (−0.038/case, a 30% cut in the edge). The threshold form also makes the EV non-monotone: raising the scrap bid 0.214->0.215 drops gross 3.6411->3.6137 (7 down-steps in a 0.001 sweep; none at bar 0), and adding a 0.5% pct bar under join='either' RAISES gross 3.6781->3.6844 (page confirms 3.6844). The per-listing-cost model is continuous in the bid (3.5617, 3.5630, 3.5672, 3.5735 at 0.213..0.216). A person sorting loot pays the attention on each listing, so the cost model matches experience; the threshold model only decides what to list.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran the finding's reproduction (bar.py, cliff.py, page_check.txt) and wrote an independent re-derivation from the raw snapshot without importing ev_ref (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/d4b26fab-cdf4-573a-8269-c661bf06e643/scratchpad/audit/refute-ev1/indep.py, output indep.txt; run: cd .../audit/refute-ev1 && python3 indep.py). Every figure reproduces exactly: page default gross 3.6781 / +3.61% / 0.379 listings per case, per-tier nets 1.5806/4.0556/13.4718/50.809/137.775/379.827 and broken 13/99/64/0/3/9% (matches README reference); fee 0.05 -> 3.6591 (+3.07%), fee 0.10 -> 3.6402 (+2.54%), fee 0.20 -> 3.6022 (+1.47%); bar 0 + fee 0.10 -> 3.6257 (+2.13%); a bar sweep 0..0.40 under fee 0.10 peaks at exactly bar 0.10; bid 0.214 -> 3.6411, 0.215 -> 3.6137 (a -0.0274 drop, -0.77% of ask); 'either' + pct 0.5 -> 3.6844 vs 3.6781. Code check: test60.html 4337 `sale=stat.median*taxMul, sells=sale>need, best=sells?sale:dis` and simDraw 4796 `net:sells?sale:dis` — no cost is ever subtracted from a listed piece; sortNeed 4437-4444 is a pure threshold. Mechanism therefore holds: the bar is a threshold, not a fee, and threshold-valuation is discontinuous in the scrap bid (my 0.001 sweep over 0.150-0.300 finds 9 decreasing steps at bar 0.10, 0 at bar 0, 0 under max(sale-0.10,dis); the finding's 7 was a different sweep range). Where it overreaches: (1) the 2.54% headline is conditional on the finding's own assumption fee = bar = 0.10. The comment at 4410-4414 never states a 0.10 fee; its 'five copper a listing' is the forgone edge per dropped listing (1.13/21.5 = 0.053 on the author's snapshot; 0.0317 = 0.671/21.17 on this one) and the claim is only that time is worth more than that, i.e. fee >= 0.05, which gives +3.07%, not +2.54%. (2) The page labels its number as gold 'after 1% tax'; attention is not gold, so the displayed 3.6781 is arithmetically correct for what it says; netting a time cost is a modelling choice the page could add, not an arithmetic error. (3) The 'either' sub-claim is not a defect: the comment at 4432-4436 documents join='either' as 'a weaker filter than either bar alone' and min(dis+0.10, dis*1.005) must lower need at tier 1 (1.3567 < 1.45), so a rise in gross is the intended semantics; the what_to_measure criterion 'adding a pct bar under either should never raise the gross' is wrong by design. (4) Verdict unchanged under any fee 0..0.20: edge stays positive (+1.47% to +3.61%), against a per-case sd of 7.06. Net: numbers and the threshold-discontinuity mechanism stand; severity should be robustness (modelling choice, verdict unchanged), and the proposed dual display (gold EV plus EV net of a user-set listing cost, valued max(sale-cost,dis)) is sound and would also remove the scrap-bid cliff.

claim_verdicts.claim: Claim 6b: 5 is the right cut for the marker
claim_verdicts.reason: Subsample test on 386 rolls with >=30 sales in 48h (d_thin.out): p90 relative error of a subsample median vs full median is 5.5% (n=1), 6.2% (n=2; median of 2 = mean), 2.7% (n=3), 2.6% (n=4), 2.2% (n=5), 1.6% (n=8), 1.4% (n=10). claim_verdicts.claim: The (2*sd/edge)^2 formula and the 'cases before profit reliably beats the swing' wording
claim_verdicts.reason: Formula is n at which edge*n = 2 SE = 2 sd sqrt(n), i.e. mean profit is two standard errors above zero; MC of 300 batches of 12,100 at unit 3.55 gives P(profit>0)=97.7%, exactly Phi(2). Wording is fair. Caveat: edge is taken at the unit price of the CURRENT caseCount (3.55 at n=1), not at the price of the 12,100 cases it recommends (unit >=3.5897, edge 0.0884, n 25,500; self-consistent fixed point 28,900) - see finding F2.

The core (non-Trends) path is correct, so the two headline figures disagree on those floors. findings.title: Swing line's 'cases before profit reliably beats the swing' uses the edge at the current caseCount, not at the n it recommends: 12,100 shown, >=25,500 at the visible book, fixed point ~28,900
findings.summary: paintCase computes need=(2*sd/edge)^2 with edge=gross-cost.unit where cost=craftWalk('case1',n) for the caseCount in the input (default 1 -> unit 3.55, edge 0.1281 -> 12,100). But 12,100 cases cannot be bought at 3.55: the visible book holds 4,766 cases up to 3.599; walking it (remainder at the 3.599 floor) gives unit 3.58966 at n=12,100, edge 0.0884, need 25,473 -> 25,500; iterating to self-consistency gives n=28,916 (unit 3.59509, edge 0.0830), itself a floor since deeper asks are unseen. The page already shows this drift when the user types n (n=1000: 13,400; n=9999: 24,400) but at the default n=1 the figure understates the requirement by 2.1-2.4x. The formula and wording are otherwise right: MC of 300 batches of 12,100 at unit 3.55 -> P(profit>0)=97.7% = Phi(2), median profit 1,616, p10 544.

findings.title: Confirmation: simulator, simPick, BigInt core, bookLevels, float sums all sound; residual nits
findings.summary: (a) Replicated simDraw equals the card's per-tier net exactly on every tier and the whole-case MC (6 x 1e6) matches gross 3.6781 within noise; there is no slot at any tier without a priced roll, so the 'unpriced -> 0 vs renormalise' divergence is latent only (it would appear only if e.g. mythic chest lost its last priced roll). (b) Within-tier dispersion adds 3% of variance: sd 7.17 vs 7.06, 12,500 vs 12,100 cases - not worth changing. (d) 0 failures in 1.8M brute-force checks; extractNumber caveats: '1,234'->1.234, '1,234,567'->null. (f) float relative error 2e-16. Nits: flipCheckCore's buyI3=Math.round(Number(shown)*1000) disagrees with toThousandths on 369 of 500,000 four-decimal inputs (x.xxx5 half cases, e.g. 0.5005 -> 500 vs 501) so the flip figure and the docket can be a tick apart on 4dp inputs; tax '1,5' parses as 0 in both Number() and dec() silently; tax '-1' is accepted by taxFrac (99/100) while paintCase/simRun clamp negatives to 0. (c) bookPanel/bookLevels correct; price-impact omission is small at 100 cases/day (knife 6.1%, helmet1 10.6% of daily volume, <1% elsewhere; scraps 825 per 100 cases vs 654,018 at best bid) and only material at the swing-line n (knife 105%, helmet1 184% of daily volume if 12,100 cases are opened over 7 days).
